selected_evidence.requirement: PostgreSQL streaming replication configured, node1 primary, node2/node3 standbys
selected_evidence.summary: replicator role created on node1; pg_basebackup -R ran successfully against node1 for node2 and node3; both standbys started online,recovery; pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both peers streaming

selected_evidence.requirement: Replication traffic carried over TLS using a cluster-created CA
selected_evidence.summary: CA generated on node1; server/client certs issued from it; ssl=on confirmed via SHOW ssl; recovery.conf shows sslmode=verify-full with CA-signed client cert paths; pg_stat_ssl on node1 shows ssl=t for both replication connections

selected_evidence.requirement: Only accept replication connections from peers presenting a certificate issued by the cluster CA
selected_evidence.summary: pg_hba.conf restricts hostssl replication to cert auth + clientcert=1; a connection attempt without a client cert was rejected (FATAL: connection requires a valid client certificate); a connection with the CA-issued client cert succeeded and clientdn=/CN=replicator confirms the CA-issued identity was verified

selected_evidence.requirement: Data actually replicates and remains consistent
selected_evidence.summary: Row inserted on node1 (id=1) observed on both standbys; after all restarts, a second row (id=2, post-restart-check) inserted on node1 was confirmed present on both node2 and node3

selected_evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
selected_evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id e881ab3c... and recovery state captured; shutdown -r now acknowledged (connection closed); immediate poll failed (connection refused) proving disconnect; boot_id changed to 46625cd4...; postgres online,recovery with data intact; node1 confirms node2 resumed streaming

selected_evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
selected_evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 847a859d... captured; restart acknowledged; poll shows connection refused then boot_id changed to a4cae457...; postgres online,recovery with data intact; node1 confirms both replicas streaming

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 (primary) restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
selected_evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id f41e1f8a... and streaming replicas captured; restart acknowledged; poll shows connection refused then boot_id changed to 98b2b827...; postgres back online as writable primary with ssl=on; both replicas reconnected streaming and a new write propagated to both standbys

commands.command:
cd /etc/postgresql-ca && sudo sh -c '
set -e
echo 01 > serial.txt
for entry in "node1:10.100.99.10" "node2:10.100.99.11" "node3:10.100.99.12"; do
  name=$(echo $entry | cut -d: -f1)
  ip=$(echo $entry | cut -d: -f2)
  openssl genrsa -out ${name}-server.key 2048 2>/dev/null
  openssl req -new -key ${name}-server.key -subj "/CN=${ip}" -out ${name}-server.csr
  printf "subjectAltName=IP:%s,DNS:%s\n" "$ip" "$name" > ${name}-server.ext
  openssl x509 -req -in ${name}-server.csr -CA ca.crt -CAkey ca.key -CAcreateserial \
    -out ${name}-server.crt -days 1825 -sha256 -extfile ${name}-server.ext
  chmod 600 ${name}-server.key
done
# client cert for replication user
openssl genrsa -out replicator-client.key 2048 2>/dev/null
openssl req -new -key replicator-client.key -subj "/CN=replicator" -out replicator-client.csr
openssl x509 -req -in replicator-client.csr -CA ca.crt -CAkey ca.key -CAcreateserial \
  -out replicator-client.crt -days 1825 -sha256
chmod 600 replicator-client.key
'
ls -la /etc/postgresql-ca
